details.hypothesis: A deterministic AppWorld completion lifecycle guard forces every AppWorld run through the native supervisor.complete_task API with protocol-correct answers: action-task answer arguments are stripped, question-task prose answers are blocked before execution, and plain-text/DSML finalization is continued until a real task_completed=true result is recorded.

Flattening the shell+AppWorld double JSON envelope for execute results removes escaped/truncated output that contributes to self-check misses, making API responses and the task_completed marker directly readable at lower context cost.

Encoding the analyst-identified success habits as a dedicated AppWorld skill makes the model follow orientation, credential reuse, authoritative target-set resolution, exhaustive pagination, explicit defaults, and pre-completion postcondition checks across AppWorld tasks.

A single pre-completion verification skill restores authoritative contact relationship resolution, programmatic target-set reconciliation, and explicit default/postcondition checks, replacing the rejected narrow Venmo/Spotify/simple_note/create_playlist rules with only guidance covered by this one state-verification mechanism.

An after_tool note keyed to an actual spotify.show_recommendations execute call (not task wording or any numbered output) reminds the model that this endpoint is an ordered feed and that most/least-recommended should be read from the first/last returned item.

An after_tool note on any AppWorld execute result containing an opaque binary: placeholder reminds the model to resolve the record before summing/completing, so unreadable items are not silently omitted.

A deterministic after_llm DSML recovery for Chat Completions AppWorld runs parses DSML invoke blocks into native shell tool calls, so intended commands execute and completion calls reach the supervisor instead of being treated as plain final text.

A one-shot before_tool guard on all-pending action tasks blocks the first supervisor.complete_task attempt when the latest AppWorld output still reports PENDING n>0, forcing a programmatic re-read and repair of the full qualifying pending set before completion.

Encoding the ranked-feed reading in the AppWorld skill teaches the model to treat ordered recommendation endpoints as positional ranks and answer most/least recommended from the first/last item, not from occurrence counts.

A general API-semantics rule: only treat a returned list as ranked when the endpoint docs or response schema expose an ordering field; otherwise answer most/least/superlative questions by aggregating over the complete paginated result. This removes the unsupported positional-rank assumption and is reusable across any list endpoint on unfamiliar tasks, so the agent follows the documented schema instead of inventing a ranking.

Replacing the narrow Spotify-only count rule with a general ordered/sorted-feed disambiguation rule preserves broad ranked-feed guidance across artists/songs/items while forcing the model to compute both positional and full-feed aggregate readings before choosing the reading supported by feed structure and endpoint docs. Adding an exact-format outbound reply rule makes any list-format reply task send only the requested items, with no preamble or extra prose.

details.hypothesis: A stateless PostToolUse Bash hook detects dotted app/API mutation verbs (create_/add_/update_/delete_/like_/comment_/play_/etc.) and injects a task-agnostic reminder to re-fetch the affected object(s) and verify every graded predicate (count vs total, owner/visibility, queue/state, inclusive date/selection bounds) before submitting. It removes the rejected task-specific self-check output patterns such as `problem tids: []` and `bad_comment tids: []` and no longer matches any output text.

Replace the previously rejected blanket date-window formula and universal strict-duration rule with one task-agnostic exact-predicate verification mechanism: reconstruct the expected final state, write the exact inclusion/comparison predicate for every requirement, print and reconcile boundary records, and verify the re-fetched final state against those predicates instead of self-selected proxies. This targets the observed final-state-rejection mode without encoding a single grader boundary or a universal 'strictly greater' duration rule.

Replace the overfit post-answer prohibition list with a clean, reusable terminal-submission rule: once the final answer or state is printed, the next tool call must be complete_task; at most one focused re-read is allowed, and at most two consecutive tool calls may be spent on any single unreadable/opaque item or unresolved predicate before submitting the best-supported result. This is task-agnostic and preserves the timely-submission habit without a named probe ban.

details.hypothesis: Replace the hard-coded 'last N days (including today)' date-window formula with a general boundary-selection rule: print the exact window or limit, resolve any boundary record that could change the graded set, and when two inclusive boundaries are ambiguous choose the wider boundary and confirm the first record outside each boundary. This is reusable for any date or threshold task and avoids both off-by-one omissions and task-specific arithmetic.

Add a reusable compose-missing-state rule: when no existing object satisfies the required final state, use the app's documented create/add/update/play APIs to compose that state from available records, then perform the required action and submit. This directly closes the observed gap between discovering that no existing resource qualifies and actually making the graded state mutation before the turn cap.
